title: Policy bundle tree index and signature (ACP-SPEC-001 §8.2)
description:
The index of one signed policy bundle: every member file, its digest, and the hybrid signature over the canonical tree.

WHY AN INDEX EXISTS AT ALL. The signature covers `SHA-256 of canonical bundle tree`. Without an explicit member list, "the tree" is whatever the reader happened to walk — so a verifier that skipped a file and a signer that included it would compute different hashes and neither could tell which was wrong. The index makes the covered set a signed fact rather than a convention, which is the same reasoning that makes tools/sign-release.sh halt on an unrecognised file type instead of silently signing or silently skipping it.

COVERAGE IS TOTAL AND CLOSED. Every file in the bundle directory MUST appear in `members`, and every member MUST exist. A file present on disk but absent from the index is a load error, not a warning — an unsigned file sitting inside a signed bundle is precisely the shape of an attack. The loader reports the first discrepancy and refuses the bundle.

members.description: Every file in the bundle, sorted by path under a byte-wise ordering. Sorting is normative: the tree hash is computed over this sequence, so two signers must agree on the order or they produce different hashes for identical content. Byte-wise, not locale-aware — a locale-dependent sort is a portability defect that only appears on someone else's machine.

path.description: Path relative to the bundle root, forward slashes. No leading slash, no `.`, no `..`, and no backslashes — a path that can escape the bundle root is a file-read primitive handed to whoever writes the index.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's exact bytes. Bytes, not parsed content: two JSON documents that parse equal but differ in whitespace are different files, and pretending otherwise reintroduces the encoding split at the file level.

signature.description:
Hybrid signature over the canonical tree hash.

CR-3, CONJUNCTIVE: verification requires EVERY declared primitive, never any. An `any`-shaped check lets an attacker strip the post-quantum signature, present a genuine classical one, and be accepted — the exact downgrade the hybrid suite exists to prevent. Proven in reference/proofs/binding.dfy: `CR3_AND_SurvivesPQBreak` versus `CR3_OR_CollapsesOnSingleBreak`.

Both fields are REQUIRED rather than optional. An optional signature field would create two canonical encodings of one object (Z4), and would also let a bundle omit the leg an attacker cannot forge.

suite.description: CR-1: a suite this build cannot verify is REFUSED, never ignored. Unsupported is not a pass.

pq.description: ML-DSA-65 signature, base64. 3309 bytes raw. ML-DSA signing is hedged (randomised) unless a deployment pins deterministic signing, which is why conformance vectors are defined over canonical bytes and declared mutations rather than over signatures.
